source: NCERT Class VIII, Resources and Development, Geography Ch. 4.

sections.heading: 1. What is Industry
points: **Industry** = an economic activity concerned with **producing goods, extracting minerals or providing services**.
It is a **secondary activity** (turning raw materials into finished goods).
Industries provide employment, add value, and drive economic development.

points.text: **By main role:** basic/key industries (supply to others, e.g. iron & steel) vs consumer industries (make goods for direct use).

sections.heading: 3. Factors Affecting Location
points: Industries locate where they get **raw materials, power (energy), labour, capital, water, transport and markets**.
Where many factors combine, **industrial regions** develop; the industry may draw a **town/city** around it.

sections.heading: 4. Major Industries
points: **Iron and Steel** — a **basic industry** (feeds many others); needs iron ore, coal, limestone (e.g. Jamshedpur — TISCO; also Pittsburgh, Ruhr).
**Textile (cotton)** — an **agro-based** industry (e.g. Ahmedabad, Mumbai; Osaka, Japan).
**Information Technology (IT)** — a modern service industry (e.g. **Bengaluru**, 'Silicon Valley of India'; Silicon Valley, California).

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Industry = secondary activity (raw materials → finished goods).
By raw material: agro-based, mineral-based, marine, forest.
Location factors: raw materials, power, labour, capital, transport, market.
Iron & steel = basic industry (Jamshedpur/TISCO); cotton textile = agro-based (Ahmedabad).
IT hub: Bengaluru ('Silicon Valley of India').

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Iron and steel** is a **basic/key industry** — it supplies raw material to many others.
Location depends on **many factors** (raw materials, power, labour, transport, market), not one alone.
